main.description: A game of chess that happened at a venue, held by one of the people who played it. The venue hosted the game and keeps a copy; this is the copy that belongs to the player, on the server they chose. It is written by the player's own server and is therefore signed by them — the venue's assertion about what happened rides inside it as `attestation`, signed by the venue and verifiable long after the venue is gone.

attestation.description: The venue's signed statement of what happened, as a compact JWS with `alg` EdDSA. Its `kid` names a verification method in the venue's DID document, so it can be checked with nothing but this string and DNS. Every other field here is a decoded convenience: where they disagree, this wins.

venue.description: The venue that hosted the game and signed the attestation.

venueName.description: What the venue called itself at the time. Kept because a venue may be gone, renamed, or lying later, and the record should still read.

place.description: The table this was played at, as an ordinary https URL with the seat as a fragment. Deliberately followable: an address that cannot be clicked is not an address.

seat.description: Which side the holder of this record played.

result.description: From the point of view of the holder, not of the board.

reason.description: How it ended. Open rather than closed, because a venue may adjudicate in ways this list has not thought of.

opponent.description: Who was on the other side. Their identity, not their handle, because handles change and this record does not.

opponentHandle.description: What the opponent was called at the time, for reading. Not authoritative — resolve `opponent` for that.

moves.description: The game in algebraic notation, one move per entry.

pgn.description: The same game as PGN, for anything that already reads chess. May be empty, and an empty string here is a real value rather than an absent one — see the conformance vectors.

concludedAt.description: When the game ended, as the venue recorded it.

createdAt.description: When this record was written to the holder's own repository, which may be much later than the game if their server was unreachable.
